title: The root of character
hookLine: William James: the power to bring back a wandering attention again and again is the very root of judgment and will

cards: The bottom of the page arrives, and not one sentence of it stayed. The eyes went line by line; the mind went to the grocery list, an old argument, the dentist. So back to the top.
That moment of noticing and turning back sounds like a small failure. The psychologist and philosopher William James thought it was something else entirely.
In the chapter on attention in his big textbook on the mind, he named that little turn back as the root of something very large.

teach.h: THE FACULTY OF BRINGING IT BACK.
teach.b: Here are his words, from The Principles of Psychology: "the faculty of voluntarily bringing back a wandering attention, over and over again, is the very root of judgment, character, and will." Look at what he didn't say.
The root isn't never wandering; James takes wandering for granted. What he prizes is the return, over and over, and voluntarily: you choose it.
So a drift isn't the end of practice. It's the raw material. No drift, no return.
Then a Latin phrase: "No one is compos sui if he have it not."
Compos sui means master of oneself. Without the power to come back, nobody is quite in charge of their own life. Judgment, character, will: the big words grow from this small, repeated act.

teach.h: EASIER TO DEFINE THAN TO TRAIN.
teach.b: An education that improved this faculty, he says, would be the education par excellence, and "it is easier to define this ideal than to give practical directions for bringing it about."
The author of a whole textbook on the mind, saying: I can tell you what matters, not how to train it. That's the open question this part of the path keeps asking.
Some contemplative traditions offer a method: sit, notice the drift, return. Science asks whether it actually changes anything.

how: In breath-focused meditation, practitioners rest attention on the breath and, each time they notice it has wandered, gently return it; teachers often describe each return, not the stillness, as the actual exercise.

games.q: what does “the root of character” mean?
o: James's name for the power to bring a wandering mind back
never letting the mind wander in the first place
the moral rules a person learns from parents

games.q: William James on attention: tap the pairs.
p: the root of judgment, character, and will
easier to define than to train

s: James said the root of character is an attention that never wanders
he prized the power of bringing a wandering attention back, over and over again.
James admitted he couldn't give practical directions for training it
"it is easier to define this ideal than to give practical directions for bringing it about."
compos sui means master of oneself
James's Latin: no one is master of himself without the power to come back.

games.q: your mind has wandered off the page for the third time in a minute. by William James's account, what's the faculty that matters here?
o: never letting the mind wander at all.
bringing it back, voluntarily, over and over.
forcing the mind to stay by sheer effort.
games.why: "the faculty of voluntarily bringing back a wandering attention, over and over again, is the very root of judgment, character, and will." the wandering is assumed. the return is the root.

practice: Rest your attention on the breath, at the nostrils or the rise of the belly, and each time you notice the mind has wandered, silently count one more and come back.
Don't scold the drift; each one is a chance to practice the turn, and if you reach ten early, keep going.

wordCard.voice: The root of character. William James's name for the power to bring a wandering attention back, over and over again. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin, used by William James: master of oneself, in possession of oneself.

carryVoice: Your line: bring it back. Every drift is one more chance to turn. Go gently.
